prs.title: Fix auto-import not offering unsaved exports after auto-imports were computed
prs.author: 1-DARK
prs.body:
Fixes #64953

   `markBucketsDirty` removed a bucket from the "clean" set after its first dirty file (when `multipleFilesDirty` was false), instead of once the
 bucket was fully dirty. Any further changed files in the same batch were then skipped.

   In the reported sequence, closing `importer.ts` and opening `exporter.ts` land in one batch. The Deleted importer was processed first, so the
 Changed `exporter.ts` was never marked dirty. The bucket kept the stale (empty) `exporter.ts`, and `unsavedFn` was never offered as an auto-import,
 via completion or `getImportEditsForSymbols`.

   The condition was inverted in three places (the project bucket and both node_modules paths). Each now removes the bucket only when
 `multipleFilesDirty` is true.

   ## Tests

   Adds `TestUnsavedExportAfterAutoImportsComputed` in `tsc/internal/ls/autoimport/registry_test.go`. It follows the reported sequence: open importer,
 request auto-imports, close importer, open exporter with unsaved content, reopen importer, request auto-imports. It then asserts that the project
 bucket indexed the export.

   - Without the fix: FAIL. The bucket is dirty only for `importer.ts` and has `ExportCount:0`.
   - With the fix: PASS.

   ```
   $ go test ./internal/ls/autoimport -run TestUnsavedExport
   ok     github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/ls/autoimport
   ```

   Other checks:
   - `go test ./internal/project/... ./internal/ls/... ./internal/fourslash/...` passes.
   - `npx hereby lint`: 0 issu

prs.title: Optimized insertion-ordered symbol tables
prs.author: ahejlsberg
prs.body:
This PR builds on #64916 to further optimize symbol tables. Symbol table entries are now just `*ast.Symbol` (half the size of #64916) and the rare renamed symbols are stored via proxy symbols that carry the new name and a reference to the original symbol.

Closes #64916

prs.author: magic-akari

prs.title: Skip non-public members when resolving reverse-mapped types
prs.author: kirkouimet
prs.body:
Fixes #64593

## Problem

Inferring `T` for `Readonly<C & T>` from a class `C` with a private member produces a `T` that redeclares that member as public. `resolveReverseMappedTypeMembers` copies every source property, and the copy carries the member's declarations but no accessibility.

Before #63932 that copy was harmless, because the intersection property resolved as private. After #63932, intersection properties take the most permissive accessibility (as `syntheticProtectedProperties.ts` asserts), so the public copy wins and `getAccount() as Account` reports TS2352. TypeScript 6.0.3 accepts the same code.

## Change

A reverse mapping recovers the source of a homomorphic mapped type, whose keys come from `keyof`. `keyof` never produces a private or protected member, since `getLiteralTypeFromProperty` returns `never` for one. So a non-public source property has no key to map from, and is skipped:

```go
if getDeclarationModifierFlagsFromSymbol(prop)&ast.ModifierFlagsNonPublicAccessibilityModifier != 0 {
    continue
}
```

This leaves #63932's accessibility rule untouched.

## Testing

- New compiler test `reverseMappedTypePrivateMembers.ts`, baselined with the repo's runner. It covers the inferred call that regressed, plus the explicit type argument and the non-generic form, which must stay clean. A private and a protected member are both included. Without the fix, the test reports the TS2352 above; with it, no errors.
- `syntheticProtectedProperties.ts`: diagnostics unch
